items.followUp: State Newton’s first law of motion.

rubric.why: The law describes bodies that are at rest.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the law deals with bodies at rest.

rubric.why: The law also describes bodies moving uniformly in a straight line.
rubric.description: Identifies bodies moving with uniform straight-line motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the law deals with bodies moving with uniform velocity in a straight line.

modelAnswer: Newton’s first law deals with bodies that are at rest or moving with uniform velocity in a straight line.

items.followUp: Why is the gravitational force between two ordinary objects difficult to notice?

rubric.why: Ordinary objects have small masses, so their mutual gravitational attraction is weak.
rubric.description: Relates the small masses of ordinary objects to their weak gravitational attraction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that ordinary objects have small masses.

rubric.why: The attraction between ordinary objects is too small to feel or notice.
rubric.description: Explains why the gravitational force is not normally perceived.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the force is too small to notice or feel.

modelAnswer: Ordinary objects have small masses, so the gravitational force between them is very small.
This force is too small for us to notice or feel.

items.followUp: Why does a passenger tend to fall backward when a bus starts suddenly?

rubric.why: The passenger’s body tends to maintain its state of motion because of inertia.
rubric.description: Identifies inertia of motion as the cause.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming inertia of motion.

rubric.why: When the bus stops, the upper body tends to continue moving forward, causing the passenger to fall forward.
rubric.description: Explains how the upper body’s continued forward motion causes the fall.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the upper body continues moving forward.

modelAnswer: When the bus brakes suddenly, the passenger’s feet and lower body stop with the bus.
The upper body tends to continue moving forward due to inertia of motion, so the passenger falls forward.
